title: The Quiet Gravity Again
premise: Beatrix Crane smuggles memories between the warring fleets of Ceres and Ganymede, hiding in the gaps of a nine-year ceasefire built on a forged transmission she helped create. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, both fleets detect the anomaly and trace it to the same buried relay station where her lie lives. To keep two armadas from annihilating each other, Beatrix must return to the station with her ragtag crew, expose her own forgery to the one person who could forgive it, and broadcast a truth that costs her the anonymity—and the family—she never believed she deserved.
about_author: Wendell Zhou is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about people living in the margins of vast systems. He lives aboard a decommissioned ferry off the coast of British Columbia with his partner and an unreasonable number of tide charts.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Mid-run between Ceres and Ganymede, Beatrix hides contraband memories in a dead courier's skull when gravity stutters for exactly nine seconds across the whole system. Her ship's AI logs a signal echo from coordinates she recognizes instantly: the relay station she falsified records from years ago. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Weight of Contraband
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Docking at Ceres, she delivers a client's stolen wedding memory and collects payment that doesn't cover the danger now following her. Fleet interrogators board her ship asking about the gravity event; she lies well but notices they already have partial telemetry. Beat: the cost of being good at disappearing.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Necessities
chapters.summary: POV Juno, her teenage navigator and de facto daughter. Juno maps the signal echo while the crew debates fleeing versus investigating: engineer Okafor, washed-up fleet pilot Sable, and archivist-medic Pell. Juno realizes Beatrix is lying about why she knows those coordinates. Beat: found family sensing a fracture before it opens.

chapters.title: What the Relay Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Flashback woven into the approach to the relay station: nine years ago, ordered to destroy evidence of a friendly-fire massacre, she instead forged a ceasefire transmission and buried the truth beneath the station's core. The gravity flicker was the station's failsafe waking up. Beat: guilt as gravity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At the station, the crew finds a Ceres boarding team already aboard—and learns Ganymede has dispatched its own. Both fleets believe the other triggered the flicker as a weapons test. Sable, a deserter from one of them, must decide whose side survival demands. Beat: loyalty under pressure.

chapters.title: The Failsafe Counts Down
chapters.summary: POV Okafor. The station's core is purging its archives to hide the massacre evidence permanently—which will also erase the forged ceasefire record, giving both fleets legal grounds to resume war. Okafor jury-rigs a way in, but every hour spent inside broadcasts their position. Beat: ingenuity against the clock.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Trapped with the Ceres boarding officer, Commander Ilsa Voss—the woman whose brother died in the massacre and whose grief Beatrix's forgery weaponized—Beatrix confesses everything. Voss must choose between justice for the dead and peace for the living. Beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Juno. With Ganymede marines breaching and both fleets' battle groups converging, the crew races to transmit the true massacre records alongside Beatrix's confession. Juno takes the transmitter chair because she's the only one small enough to reach the junction—her first act of real courage. Beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Fall Together
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The truth goes out; both fleets stand down in stunned silence, then turn their fury on the messenger. Beatrix surrenders herself to Voss to buy the crew time to escape, finally paying the debt she's carried for nine years. Beat: sacrifice as belonging—she gives herself up so her family can be free.

chapters.title: Gravity, Holding
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Months later, the ceasefire holds on honest terms, fragile but real. Beatrix, pardoned for her confession, returns to a repaired ship where the crew waited without being asked. Juno logs them in as family, not crew. Beat: quiet resolution—the weight that holds you can also be home.
